programme.title: 7 Up: The Story
programme.desc: In 1964, ITV broadcast a film about fourteen seven-year-olds. It became the longest running documentary series ever. Those children are now seventy. 7 Up set out to prove that Britain was divided by the class system - that these children's futures had been decided by the street they were born on. The production team had three weeks to find them. They went to some of the poorest parts of the country and some of the most privileged, and came back with ten boys and four girls. The series became one of British television's most remarkable social experiments, the cameras dipping into their lives every seven years. Children from different parts of the class system who have now become friends. This special programme looks at the year 7 Up was made, the idea behind it, and what they hoped for in a Britain about to change around them.

programme.desc: On a remote island, a wealthy entrepreneur creates a theme park featuring living dinosaurs drawn from prehistoric DNA. programme.desc: A wisecracking parrot caged in a research lab tells his life story to a lonely janitor. Touched by his colourful story, the janitor conspires to liberate the talking bird.

programme.desc: Perennial family favourite about Dorothy, a young girl from the American Midwest, who is swept by a cyclone to a magical kingdom over the rainbow. There she meets a scarecrow, a tin man and a cowardly lion, who join her on a quest to find the all-powerful Wizard of Oz, the only man who can help her get back to Kansas. However, the Wicked Witch of the West has other plans for Dorothy and her new friends.

Twenty-six years later, two children find the game in their attic, and when they start to play, Alan is released, but the game isn't over yet, and Alan must finish before he is really free.

programme.desc: A ten-year-old boy befriends and shelters a gentle alien creature who has been stranded on Earth. When the authorities are alerted to this unusual house guest, the boy tries to help the creature return home before menacing government agents close in. The film won three Academy Awards for music, sound and special effects.

programme.title: Annie

programme.desc: An alcoholic millionaire is threatened with losing his inheritance if he does not marry the girl of his parents' choosing. Despite his dislike for his prospective bride, he bows to the inevitable only to meet a light-fingered waitress who steals his heart. John Gielgud won an Oscar for his role as Arthur's loyal but outspoken valet.

programme.desc: Danny Noonan, a teen down on his luck, works as a caddy at the snob-infested Bushwood Country Club to raise money for his college education. In an attempt to gain votes for a college scholarship reserved for caddies, Noonan volunteers to caddy for a prominent and influential club member. Meanwhile, Danny struggles to prepare for the high pressure Caddy Day golf tournament while absorbing New Age advice from wealthy golf guru Ty Webb.

programme.title: Singin' in the Rain
programme.desc: When the transition is being made from silent films to `talkies', everyone has trouble adapting. Don and Lina have been cast repeatedly as a romantic couple, but when their latest film is remade into a musical, only Don has the voice for the new singing part. After a lot of practise with a diction coach, Lina still sounds terrible, and Kathy, a bright young aspiring actress, is hired to record over her voice.

programme.title: Tootsie
programme.desc: An out-of-work actor dresses in drag for an audition, only to land the female lead in a TV soap. When he becomes the most popular character on the show, he feels compelled to carry the persona into his everyday life. While bringing him phenomenal success as an `actress', life as a woman also has its problems - especially when he falls for an actress with whom he works.

His temperament leads him to anger management class, where he meets fellow misfits Chuck and Bomb. Red becomes even more agitated when his feathered brethren welcome green pigs to their island paradise. As the swine begin to get under his skin, Red joins forces with Chuck and Bomb to investigate the real reason behind their mysterious arrival.

programme.desc: Red, Chuck, Bomb and the rest of their feathered friends are surprised when a green pig suggests that they put aside their differences and unite to fight a common threat. Aggressive birds from an island covered in ice are planning to use an elaborate weapon to destroy the fowl and swine way of life. After picking their best and brightest, the birds and pigs come up with a scheme to infiltrate the island, deactivate the device and return to their respective paradises intact.

programme.title: The Cinema List: Family Favourites

programme.desc: It's Erin Burnett's turn to step out front and try to maintain a viable viewer presence for CNN in the weekday news arena. But the former CNBC anchor won't worry about ratings for her hourlong general news program, comparing that burden to "death." Instead, she'll concern herself with translating world events into relevant information for viewers, paying close attention to such topics as the Middle East and women's issues. "I want people to say that our show is smart. I want our show to be authentic", Burnett says in a promo. "I want our show to have courage". Left unsaid, of course, is that she wants her show to have a big audience, too.

programme.title: Smerconish
programme.desc: After serving as an MSNBC contributor and guest-host on the network for four years, TV and radio personality Michael Smerconish believed he was ready to head a show of his own. CNN agreed, and thus was born `Smerconish', an hourlong Saturday morning program that takes after its host's independent views. Using a topical, conversational format, he aims for the TV show to be an extension of his weekday radio broadcast, with free-flowing topics and the ability to discuss issues that strike a chord with the audience. Along the same lines, he thinks it's important to present the content in an engaging manner, free of my-way-or-the-highway ideology. Smerconish, who has a law degree from the University of Pennsylvania, is also a New York Times' best-selling author.

programme.desc: Duggee is blowing up balloons for Tino the artistic mouse's birthday. When they give the tiny mouse a big bunch of balloons, something unexpected happens. Tino starts to float up into the sky! He's having a rather good time until he gets stuck in a tree. It's time for the squirrels to come to his rescue.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: When Gadabout and Pearl lose the cure for Madam Dragon's missing flame, Zog helps them work together to assist his former teacher.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Emperor Penguin visits the berg's lookout to shed his feathers in private. But when he gets locked out in the buff, the Piris must come to the rescue to spare his blushes.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi conjures a unicorn for adventures but realises even heroes need to rest.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Cosima and Big Lizard are helping Dad train for his astronaut fitness test. When Rex gets into trouble, Dad's hard work finally pays off.

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Wanting to get his very own Octo-Watch and make his brother proud, Pinto helps Dashi on some missions with Paani and Koshi.

programme.title: Knee High Spies
programme.desc: Lauchie plans to bring Moss to take-your-pet-to-school day, but a jealous Silver Paw turtle-naps her. Can Jeremy and Deena find her in time for the morning school run?

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes search for honeysuckle, leaving behind a trail of berries to help find their way back. But when Wasabi eats the trail, they're stranded in the dark.

programme.title: GiggleQuiz
programme.desc: Joining Gail and Keith for today's GiggleQuiz are the Lost Pirate and Ann Teak. Keith finds an old stick under his desk, and Ann Teak gives her 'expert' opinion on what it is. Ann declares that the artefact must be a conductor's baton and demonstrates how to use it. Unbeknownst to Ann, the stick is actually a magic wand and waving it around causes Arthur's phone to turn into a pineapple. Throughout the third round, Ann Teak obliviously performs her own magic spells in the studio.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Chip sings a heartfelt song about being a potato. Though he can't do many physical things, he is proud of who he is.

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack's stall. She chooses the cinema ticket and remembers the day she got it. Alice is telling the kids a story at the Kids Club. Molly thinks her dad, James, and Alice are getting on very well. When Bob finds an old film projector at a jumble sale, Molly has an idea. She tells Mack that she wants James and Alice to get married! Mack explains that adults can't just get married; they have to have a date first.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Ryan's mum is Vietnamese, and he is cooking a dish from Vietnam that she has taught him. He works hard in the kitchen mixing lots of ingredients together, including pork, prawns and fresh mint. He even finds time to teach us the Vietnamese word for egg! One of Ryan's ingredients is fresh mint, but not all of Ryan's friends like the taste or smell of it at first.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how puddles play an important role in the environment. They find out that puddles are part of the water cycle and that they can support birds, animals, insects and plants too. They learn how raindrops and lakes can be a bit like puddles, and on the way, there is plenty of puddle-splashing fun to be had.

programme.title: Down on the Farm
programme.desc: Storm goes to East Lothian where lobsters are growing, JB discovers how computers and spiders help cucumbers grow on a farm in Essex, and some children from a beach club in Scotland comb the sand to help the wildlife.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: When Jess takes Evie for her first school visit, Waffle goes along too, on the condition that he doesn't sing. He tries his best to behave, but it's hard for a Wonder Dog! On their walk to school, Jess and Evie bump into Connie Lester and her daughter Ruby. Ruby reveals that she will also be starting at Sommersby School too, in the year above Evie. Ruby enjoys stroking Waffle and tells Evie that she loves animals. She has a pet dog of her own, Jelly, a yellow Labrador.

programme.title: Hey Duggee

programme.title: The Life and Death of Colonel Blimp
programme.desc: A British epic about the life and loves of a reactionary army officer, Clive Candy VC, told episodically in flashback. From his dashing career in the Boer War of 1902, the film follows Candy through marriage during the First World War to the Blitz of 1943, when he searches London for his lost youth and loves.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden
programme.desc: Marcus Wareing embraces a slower pace of life down at his Sussex smallholding. Setting out to expand the range of produce and bring in new livestock, his first additions are some new pigs, but he needs to choose animals that will provide him with the best possible meat. He heads to North Yorkshire to meet the rare Mangalitza pigs, who are famed for their deep flavour and fun personalities.

programme.title: Nadiya's Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Inspired by a lockdown social media craze, a traditional coffee cake is transformed by a light dalgona coffee cream topping, which doesn't actually contain any cream. Nadiya then shares her meringue lollipops, which have a colourfully striped crisp shell and a raspberry-infused white chocolate centre.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: Three teams, one beach, six hours to build the ultimate sandcastle. Who will sculpt to glory before the tide washes it all away in the grand final?

programme.title: Lover Come Back
programme.desc: An ambitious advertising executive is determined to win an account from her rival - not knowing that he has fabricated a non-existent product.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Anita and James discover Staffordshire ceramic dogs in Sheffield, and Paul gets to meet Pete Goss, the only person in Britain still forging surgical steel instruments by hand.

programme.title: Live: Super League Rugby
programme.desc: Live action from the play-off semi-finals as the grand final draws near.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve journeys through the lost world of Papua New Guinea's tropical rainforest, in search of the tenkile tree kangaroo, one of the rarest animals on Earth.

programme.title: Chrissie Hynde and the Pretenders at the BBC
programme.desc: With her unique voice and sense of style, Chrissie Hynde has been one of rock's most iconic stars since the punk era, when she first formed The Pretenders back in 1978. With Chrissie at the forefront, the band combined credibility with chart success, and here the very best of their performances at the BBC over the years are featured, from their number one hit Brass in Pocket to classics like I'll Stand By You, Don't Get Me Wrong and the enduring Christmas hit 2000 Miles. The collection also includes Chrissie's work outside the band, featuring performances with Rufus Wainwright, Neneh Cherry and Cher, and of course her old mates UB40 - the group she helped propel to chart success - and their huge hits Breakfast in Bed and I Got You Babe.

programme.title: Glastonbury
programme.desc: The English-American rock band deliver a smashing set, 35 years after they first formed.

programme.title: Arena

programme.title: Nostalgia
programme.desc: After forty years spent between Lebanon and Egypt, the entrepreneur Felice returns to Naples. Here he meets Don Luigi, a priest who fights the Camorra and tries to give a better future to the young people of the town.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Ash meets Gordon to drop Colin off, and they're unsure where they stand. Ash joins a sexy game night at the share house just as Gordon shows up to check on Colin.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood explores a host of gardening subjects that all begin with the letter V, getting advice from some of the BBC's most popular gardening presenters and programmes.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden's balloon odyssey takes her to the Borders region of Scotland, where she discovers the role art and literature play in creating memorable gardens. At Sir Walter Scott's Abbotsford she tries her hand at fly-fishing and meets Jeannette, whose family history there spans a century. At Little Sparta she explores a garden poem. And we hear how the Royal Botanic Garden in Edinburgh came into being.

programme.title: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
programme.desc: Student Travis Francis admits his mum does all the cooking, now he wants to cook for her. Lorraine creates a menu inspired by his family's Caribbean roots, including a prawn, sweet potato and mango curry.

programme.title: Nigel and Adam's Farm Kitchen
programme.desc: Nigel and Adam look at the disappearing notion of seasonality. With imports and technology allowing us to eat whatever we want, all year round, the boys aim to put us back in touch with nature's food cycle.

programme.title: The 39 Steps
programme.desc: Richard Hannay, pursued by the police for a murder he did not commit, and by an international spy-ring for information he does not possess, finds himself fleeing across the desolate Scottish moors, handcuffed to a beautiful blonde.
